question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in per-message timestamps to the core TUI, and should the control be persisted config, an in-session toggle, or both?
rationale: The source-visible gap is clear, but adding a timestamp display control changes user-facing TUI behavior and may add config/default surface, so automation should not choose the permanent UX contract alone.

options.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
options.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, uses real message timestamps across live streaming and history replay, and includes PTY-visible proof.

options.title: Prefer a session-only toggle
options.body: Avoid growing persistent config and accept only an in-session TUI command or UI control if maintainers want a lighter surface.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the TUI visually minimal and leave timing inspection to logs, session metadata, or a future broader transcript view.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in TUI timestamps
recommendation.body: Allow a narrow implementation that keeps timestamps disabled by default, uses real message timestamps across live streaming and history replay, and includes PTY-visible proof.
